conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Typewriter
style.description: A generic mid-century manual typewriter (no brand marks) on a pale wooden desk in daylight, shot close: sea-green enamel body, round cream keys in chrome rings, a U-shaped basket of steel type bars, a two-colour inked ribbon between two spools, cream paper on a black rubber platen. Words appear on the paper one struck letter at a time: the key dips, its type bar swings up and hits the print point, the ribbon lifts, the inked glyph is there when the bar falls back, and the carriage steps one column left. At the end of a line the bell rings, the lever throws the carriage back and the paper feeds up a line. Every strike, space, bell, ratchet tick and carriage stop is a sound cue from the same typing plan that drives the picture.
motion: One struck letter at a time: key dips, its type bar swings from the basket to the print point (about 0.1 s up, 0.14 s back), the ribbon lifts, the glyph is on the paper when the bar falls away, the carriage steps one column left.
Line end: bell, then the return lever throws the carriage back to the left margin (0.5 s) while the platen ratchets the paper up one line.
Strike times are snapped to frames so the bar is at the paper on a rendered frame; nothing eases in or fades — ink is either struck or not.
Camera: slow moves fitted to the page + machine; it follows the carriage smoothly, never the single steps.

notes.mechanism: typeplan.js: text -> per-character strike times snapped to frames, key + type bar per character, carriage column, line feeds, bell; picture and SCORE read the same plan.
